briefing.opening: Good morning/afternoon. I will now begin the daily briefing by the Climate Change Spokesperson on August 27, 2026.

sections.title: 🔴 Himalayan Catastrophe: Glacier Collapse and Flash Floods Caused by Climate Change
sections.content: Recently, in the Nepalese Himalayan region, a massive landslide and flash floods caused by glacier collapse occurred without a single drop of rain, resulting in 1,650 to 1,800 fatalities and missing persons [1, 8, 15, 115]. This incident is attributed not to an earthquake, but to the accelerated melting of glaciers due to climate change (twice as fast) and the collapse of a massive 600m glacier. Experts warn that climate change has increased the risk of such destructive floods [4, 5, 18, 19, 22, 23, 28, 29, 32, 115, 158, 159, 161]. Nine South Koreans were reported missing, but some have been safely evacuated, with 4 rescued after the dispatch of a government rapid response team [118, 121]. The Dalai Lama mourned the victims and emphasized the need for follow-up measures to prepare for climate change [9].

sections.title: ⚠️ Strengthening El Niño and Global Extreme Weather Warnings
sections.content: Due to global warming, the El Niño phenomenon is being 'supercharged' and intensifying with unprecedented strength. Research indicates that this is not merely a natural phenomenon, but that climate change has increased its frequency and intensity [2, 27, 123, 133, 135, 141, 142, 147, 152, 155, 162]. The intensification of El Niño has been proven through Galapagos coral records, leading to mentions of phenomena where 'the ocean is burning' [27, 135, 142]. A study has also revealed that 560 million children worldwide are exposed to an additional month of heat stress, suggesting that climate change poses a disproportionate heat threat to children [149, 154]. Across the globe, various regions are suffering from extreme weather events such as heavy rainfall, heatwaves, and glacier collapses [30].

sections.title: 🌱 Legalization of Carbon Neutrality Targets and Acceleration of Renewable Energy Transition
sections.content: There has been positive progress with the amendment to the Carbon Neutrality Framework Act passing the National Assembly, legalizing the goal of reducing greenhouse gas emissions by 53-61% by 2035 [42, 43, 58]. Simultaneously, a PPA brokerage platform for direct renewable energy power trading has officially launched, with contracts totaling 210MW signed. SK E&S also signed an agreement to supply 170MW of renewable energy to Samsung Biologics [59, 61, 63, 64, 66, 70, 71, 76, 89, 97, 100, 101, 105]. Gyeonggi Province is pursuing a policy aimed at securing 10GW of renewable energy to strengthen the competitiveness of its semiconductor industry [60, 81, 88], and Korea Western Power is expanding international cooperation, becoming the first domestic public power generation company to actively venture into the Central Asian renewable energy market [67, 80, 83, 93, 103, 108]. Concurrently, the '2026 Korea Wood Industry Expo,' promoting the value of domestic timber and the importance of carbon neutrality, has opened in Daejeon [33, 34, 35, 55].

sections.title: 🇰🇷 Current State of Domestic and International Climate Change Policies and Awareness
sections.content: Regarding the passage of the Carbon Neutrality Act amendment, civic groups have protested, arguing that the burden of reduction will be passed on to future generations, and that the current Nationally Determined Contribution (NDC) is insufficient [38, 44, 46, 57]. Meanwhile, the government has confirmed the construction of five new dams under the pretext of climate response [7, 116], and there have been criticisms that the Korea Meteorological Administration's credibility issues stem from 'lack of communication' rather than 'climate change' itself [6]. Internationally, the sole climate scientist at West Point, the U.S. Military Academy, was fired for teaching human-caused climate change [124, 164], and in Florida, publishers are being pressured to reduce climate change content in textbooks, indicating ongoing controversy over climate change education [134]. A French astronaut raised awareness by stating that climate change is clearly observable even from space [136, 144, 156].

briefing.closing: As we have seen in today's briefing, the world is facing the severe impacts of climate change, while simultaneously accelerating efforts towards carbon neutrality and the transition to renewable energy. This is a critical juncture where balanced development in domestic and international policies and public awareness for responding to the climate crisis becomes even more important. This concludes today's climate briefing.
